fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Operator ruling received (see comment): **"Unreadable config should result in an error."**
This settles the question this ticket was filed to carry — the opt-in `verify.*` gates must
NOT keep failing OPEN on an unreadable config, and must NOT fail closed into a
blocked-`unavailable` verdict either. An unreadable/corrupt `rebar.toml` is a FAULT the
operator must see and fix; today `gate_enabled` (`_commands/gates.py`) swallows the
`ConfigError` into `GateState.UNREADABLE`, prints one stderr warning, and the gated
operation silently proceeds as if the gate were off.

## Approach

Raise the error at the SOURCE, so every gate consumer gets the new posture without
per-caller re-implementation:

1. `gates.gate_enabled` stops catching `ConfigError` into `GateState.UNREADABLE`. On an
   unreadable config it raises a `ConfigError` (chained `from` the parse fault) naming the
   gate label, the ticket, and the underlying parse error — the existing typed config-fault
   family, so callers and tests can catch it precisely.
2. `GateState.UNREADABLE` is removed (it becomes unreachable); `GateState` keeps
   `ENABLED`/`DISABLED` and its `__bool__` so the ~15 test modules that monkeypatch
   `gate_enabled` with a plain bool keep working. The `unreadable` skip verdict branch in
   `close_plan_review_gate_check` is removed (dead); the `gate_ran` stamp and predicate
   stay (still distinguish the `disabled` skip from a gate that ran).
3. The `extra` parameter of `gate_enabled` (a warning-suffix clause) is dropped with the
   warning it decorated; both call sites passing it are updated.
4. CLI surfacing: `_cli/__init__.py main()` gains an `except ConfigError` boundary
   (alongside `RemovedInputError`/`TrackerRootError`) printing `Error: <msg>` to stderr
   with exit 1, so the new error is a clean operator-facing failure, not a traceback —
   the same rendering `main()` already gives a `ConfigError` from `-c` overrides.
5. Docs updated to the new contract: `docs/plan-review-gate.md` (the "unreadable config
   fails this opt-in gate off with a warning" paragraph), `docs/config.md` bullet 6
   ("Loud, not silent"), `docs/llm-framework.md`'s matching sentence.

### Caller sweep (every `gate_enabled` consumer, per c504977aef's RCA)

- `gates.close_plan_review_gate_check` (plan-review close gate) — PROPAGATES. Called
  pre-lock by `transition_close`, so the error is raised BEFORE `txn.transition_core`
  takes the write lock; the b8841ae695 property (an unreadable config does no work under
  the lock) is preserved and stays tested. The in-lock recheck closure is only installed
  after a pre-lock check that RAN. Precision on the rare pre-lock→lock window (the config
  turns unreadable AFTER a passing pre-lock check): the locked recheck's `ConfigError` is
  re-typed by `transition_core`'s fail-closed boundary (`txn.py`: `except Exception →
  CommandError(f"Error: {exc}", returncode=1) from None`), so THAT path aborts loudly as
  a `CommandError` carrying the parse-fault text in its message — exit 1, close refused —
  but NOT as the typed, chained `ConfigError` and NOT via the CLI `ConfigError` boundary.
  That is deliberate: `transition_core`'s re-wrap is its existing fail-closed contract
  for the write path and is out of scope here; the typed, chained `ConfigError`
  guarantee (AC1/AC2) applies to the pre-lock and claim paths, which are the paths an
  unreadable-at-operation-start config actually takes.
- `gates._plan_review_gate_applies` → `plan_review_precheck` (claim + `transition open
  in_progress`) and `claim.py` stage-1 `--review` sensing — PROPAGATES: starting work on
  an unreadable config fails loudly.
- `close_precheck._completion_precheck` (completion close gate) — PROPAGATES: the close
  fails loudly before any billable verifier work.
- `gates.description_cap_warning` — DELIBERATE CATCH, kept: its `except Exception →
  None` guards an advisory-only notice emitted after a write has already committed
  (documented in its docstring and pinned by
  `test_description_cap_warning.py::test_an_unreadable_cap_never_disturbs_the_write`).
  The ruling scopes the error to gate resolution of gated operations; the completed
  write must not be disturbed, and the actual claim of that ticket still errors.

Read-only ops (`list`, `show`, `search`) do not resolve gates and are unaffected — the
error is scoped to gate resolution, exactly as the ruling demands.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py` — the raise, `GateState` narrowing, docstrings.
- `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — call-site signature + comment.
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — comment describing the recheck-install
  condition (behavioural text references the retired unreadable skip).
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` — the `ConfigError` boundary in `main()`.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/config.md`, `docs/llm-framework.md` — contract text.
- Tests: rewrite `tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_close_gate_ran_predicate_2091.py` (unreadable arm),
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py`; new RED module
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_gate_unreadable_config_errors_39f8.py`.

## Testing

RED before GREEN (the new module fails on current main, passes after):

- Happy/failure pair at the function: readable-on → `ENABLED`, readable-off →
  `DISABLED`; malformed `rebar.toml` → `ConfigError` raised, message names the gate
  label, the ticket id, and the parse fault.
- End-to-end failure paths: with a malformed `rebar.toml`, (a) `rebar.claim` fails
  loudly naming the config fault and the ticket stays `open`; (b) a close via
  `rebar.transition(in_progress→closed)` fails loudly BEFORE the write lock (the ticket
  stays `in_progress`, no status event is appended, and the in-lock recheck is never
  invoked — the b8841ae695 no-work-under-the-lock property, retargeted from "silently
  proceeds" to "errors first").
- Invariance guards: `disabled` skip verdict, `gate_ran` stamp semantics, and bool
  monkeypatch compatibility unchanged.
- Full gates: `make lint`, targeted pytest for the modules above, `make typecheck`,
  complexity ratchet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a malformed `rebar.toml`, `gate_enabled` raises `ConfigError` (chained from
  the parse fault, message naming gate + ticket + fault) instead of returning a state —
  checked by `tests/unit/test_gate_state_tristate_f5c4.py`.
- [ ] With a malformed `rebar.toml`, a claim fails loudly with that error (exit ≠ 0 on
  the CLI, typed raise in the library) leaving the ticket `open` — checked by
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_gate_unreadable_config_errors_39f8.py`.
- [ ] With a malformed `rebar.toml`, a close fails loudly with that error leaving the
  ticket `in_progress` — checked by the same new test module.
- [ ] The close-path error is raised BEFORE the write lock; no config read or gate work
  happens under the lock on the unreadable path — checked by the rewritten
  `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_close_gate_unreadable_config_2091.py`.
- [ ] A readable config's behaviour is byte-identical (`ENABLED`/`DISABLED` resolution,
  the `disabled` skip verdict, the `gate_ran` stamp, bool monkeypatch compatibility) —
  checked by the existing gate test suites staying green.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `docs/config.md`, and `docs/llm-framework.md` state
  the new contract (unreadable config ⇒ error; never a silent skip, never a fake
  `disabled`) — checked by reading the three updated sections.
